analysis:
Examined the ServingReadiness.swift verdict refactor (head lines 47-141), the new ProviderOperationalMessage case coordinatorRefusalUnconfirmed (ProviderLogger.swift:149), and the new .inferenceRequest event handler in ProviderLoop+Serve.swift (head lines 429-432).

Security-relevant behavior: ServingReadiness is diagnostic plus a re-registration trigger (ProviderLoop.superviseServingAuthorization, not in the supplied evidence). It does not grant or extend serving authorization. The coordinator keeps authority through the T-053 final-handoff recheck and TB-011 grants. The new .unconfirmed verdict is a stale-refusal state. A refusal older than refusalMaxAge (60s) no longer yields .blocked. If the supervisor treats only .blocked as grounds for re-registration, a stale refusal could delay a re-register. That is an availability and diagnostic effect, not an authorization bypass. The change reflects an intent to avoid spurious re-registration loops, which bears on T-057 and A-018.

The new 'routed' path reports .authorized when lastRequestAt is later than trust.receivedAt. It is derived only from a coordinator-sent inferenceRequest event, so it is coordinator-originated on the TB-002 channel. It is used as a local diagnostic and does not influence coordinator routing. An adversarial consumer or provider cannot forge it locally. The remaining risk is cosmetic: a status line may say 'authorized' on the strength of one routed request.

The new log message is a fixed, closed-vocabulary enum case with no associated values, preserving the public-log privacy contract. The added reason string in verdict messages comes from the coordinator's authorization.reason and is rendered in diagnostics only. The public log vocabulary is untouched.

Open integration questions, not verified here because those sources were not supplied: (1) how superviseServingAuthorization handles .unconfirmed and .pending, and whether the 15-minute re-register timer still fires for a genuinely unauthorized connection; (2) the noteCoordinatorRequest implementation and where lastRequestAt is persisted in DaemonState; (3) whether the DaemonState.Trust.receivedAt field is set locally and not coordinator-controlled. No concrete regression is identified from the supplied evidence.
